==English== {{wp|}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|tast||obsolete}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*teh₂g-|id=touch}} The verb is from {{inh|en|enm|tasten}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|taster||to taste, touch or hit}}, from [[unattested]] {{der|en|la-vul|*tastāre||to touch or feel}}, from {{m|la-vul||*taxitāre}}, an [[w:Innovation (linguistics)|innovated]] {{lg|iterative}} form of {{der|en|la-cla|taxo|taxāre|to touch sharply}}, from {{m|la|tango|tangere|to touch, to grasp}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*teh₂g-|id=touch}}, which is assumed to have had the same meaning as {{m|la||tangere}}.
The noun came from the verb, and the two [[conflate]]d after English lost its [[infinitive]] suffix {{m|en|-en|id=verb ending}}, though {{m|enm|tasten}} was most likely already used [[nominatively]] (as a {{lg|gerund}}), similar to {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|tasting}}. Almost fully {{displaced|en|''native'' [[smack]]|nocap=1|sl=1}}, from {{ncog|enm|smac,smak,smacke}}, from {{ncog|ang|smæc,smæċċ||taste, smatch}}.
{{displaced|en|smatch}}, from {{ncog|enm|smacchen,smecchen}}, from {{ncog|ang|smæċċan||to taste; to smack}}; displaced also {{ncog|enm|buriȝen}}, from {{ncog|ang|bierġan||to taste}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/teɪst/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-taste.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪst|s=1}} ====Noun==== {{wikidata lexeme|L524}} {{en-noun|~}} # One of the [[sensation]]s produced by the [[tongue]] in response to certain [[chemical]]s; the quality of giving this sensation. #: {{ux|en|He had a strange '''taste''' in his mouth.}} #: {{ux|en|Venison has a strong '''taste'''.}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Rebecca Wallwork|title=‘You had to be there’: Foods that taste better on home turf|url=https://www.cnn.com/travel/foods-that-dont-travel-well|date=2023-06-15|passage=Like smell, '''taste''' has been found to imprint our minds with strong memories.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20231222140829/https://www.cnn.com/travel/foods-that-dont-travel-well|archivedate=22 December 2023}} # The [[sense]] that consists in the perception and interpretation of this sensation. #: {{ux|en|His '''taste''' was impaired by an illness.}} # A small [[sample]] of [[food]], [[drink]], or [[recreational drug]]s. # {{lb|en|countable|and|uncountable}} A person's [[implicit]] set of preferences, especially [[esthetic]], though also [[culinary]], [[sartorial]], etc. #: {{syn|en|palate}} #: {{ux|en|Dr. Parker has good '''taste''' in wine.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1777|author=w:Richard Brinsley Sheridan|title=The School for Scandal|section=II.i |passage=That's very true indeed Sir Peter! after having married you I should never pretend to '''Taste''' again I allow.}} #* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|VIII|passage="My '''tastes'''," he said, still smiling, "incline me to the garishly sunlit side of this planet." And, to tease her and arouse her to combat: "I prefer a farandole to a nocturne; I'd rather have a painting than an etching; Mr. Whistler bores me with his monochromatic mud; I don't like dull colours, dull sounds, dull intellects;{{nb...}}."}} #* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=1|passage=The huge square box, parquet-floored and high-ceilinged, had been arranged to display a suite of bedroom furniture designed and made in the halcyon days of the last quarter of the nineteenth century, when modish '''taste''' was just due to go clean out of fashion for the best part of the next hundred years.}} # Personal [[preference]]; [[liking]]; [[predilection]]. #: {{syn|en|palate}} #: {{ux|en|I have developed a '''taste''' for fine wine.}} # {{lb|en|figuratively}} A small amount of [[experience]] with something that gives a sense of its [[quality]] as a whole. #: {{ux|en|Such anecdotes give one a '''taste''' of life on a trauma ward.}} #* {{quote-av|en|date=1980-03-03|writers=w:Antony Jay; w:Jonathan Lynn|episode=w:Official Secrets (Yes, Prime Minister)|title=w:Yes, Prime Minister|season=2|number=2|role=w:Humphrey Appleby; w:Bernard Woolley|actor=w:Nigel Hawthorne; w:Derek Fowlds|passage=Sir Humphrey Appleby: Bernard, what do you want? / Bernard Woolley: I want to have a clear conscience. / {{...}} / Sir Humphrey Appleby: When did you acquire this '''taste''' for luxuries ([[laugh track]])?}} #* {{quote-song|en|author=w:KT Tunstall|title=w:Saving My Face|album=w:Drastic Fantastic|year=2007|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3W4Elr3CnXE|text=I'm all out of luck / I'm all out of faith / I would give everything just for one '''taste''' / But everything's here, all out of place{{...}}}} # A kind of narrow and thin [[silk]] [[ribbon]]. # {{lb|en|dialect}} The least [[amount]] or [[portion]] of something; a [[jot]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1850|author=w:Thomas Keightley|title=The Fairy Mythology|location=London|publisher=H.G. Bohn|page=383|passage="So he opened the door very quitely, an' didn't make a '''taste''' o' n'ise in the wurld, an' luked all about, but the niver a bit o' the little man cud he see anywhare, but he h'ard his hammerin' and whis'lin', an' so he luked and luked, till at last he seen the little fellow[.]"}} =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|sensation produced by the tongue}} {{l|en|smack}},
